title: Webb County Seeks Bids for Water Generators to Bring Drinking Water to Colonias
excerpt: Webb County commissioners approved advertising for bids on atmospheric water generators that pull drinking water from the air for families in colonias along Highway 59 and in South Webb County.
content:
Webb County is moving ahead with a plan to make drinking water from the air. On Monday, commissioners approved advertising for bids on atmospheric water generators, according to KGNS.

The machines pull moisture from the air, then filter and treat it into drinking water for families in underserved colonias.

The project is backed by a $330,000 federal award from the Southwest Border Regional Commission, announced in September by U.S. Rep. Henry Cuellar. With $82,510 in matching money from Webb County, the total investment is $412,510.

The funding will support 220 atmospheric water generators for low-income households across 18 colonias along Highway 59 and in South Webb County, along with five years of replacement filters and the administration and program support needed to carry out the project, according to Cuellar’s office.

County officials estimate the program will reach roughly 1,300 residents across about 210 households, according to Local National. Families of up to four would receive one generator, while households of five or more would receive two.

Precinct 2 Commissioner Rosaura “Wawi” Tijerina has described the generators as a stopgap while the county works toward permanent water infrastructure. “This, in the meantime, will provide drinking water to all these families,” she said.

The effort expands on a smaller pilot program the county launched last year.

Sources: KGNS, Nov. 27, 2026; U.S. Rep. Henry Cuellar, Sept. 27, 2026; Local National, Oct. 7, 2026.
